title: [RFC] Feedback on Python 3.13t (64-bit, freethreaded) Support in ONNX
body:
# Ask a Question

### Question
Do we need a 3.13t version [Python 3.13 (64-bit, freethreaded)]?

The upcoming pytorch version 2.6 will have experimental support for that:
(https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/RELEASE.md#release-compatibility-matrix)

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Sounds like a good idea if not too hard to add?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Do you know how one can create this wheel?

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: 3.13 compilation seems to be broken at the moment. Is this gonna fix it?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
@participant2 1.17 release does not contain python 3.13 support.

The next release 1.18 will contain 3.13 support (It was added with the following PR: https://github.com/onnx/onnx/pull/6370). You can install the weekly dev build from https://pypi.org/project/onnx-weekly/

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
Thanks. Any clue when this will be public? It's breaking a package that I don't maintain and I don't understand how to change from onnx to onnx-weekly with poetry.

(the package is Immich)

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: At the moment no date is set for the 1.18 release. Some discussion which relates to the release process could be found here: https://github.com/onnx/onnx/issues/6298 feel free to join

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: To come back to the original question, I haven't converted anything to python 3.13t yet, but it would be a new workflow and therefore not that easy to add. E.g. through https://github.com/actions/setup-python/issues/771 alone. Pytorch already supplies a 3.13t version.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body: Now that PR #6706 has been merged, are there any plans for 1.18 release? Reason: we can already use the wheels through `onnx-weekly` or by building it manually, but `onnxruntime-gpu` still requires 1.17, which doesn't have py3.13 support yet (afaik). So if onnx releases, onnxruntime will likely follow it shortly after and that will allow us to test py3.13 and py3.13t (freethread) as soon as possible. Currently I can't switch all my project to py3.13 only due to onnx dependencies.

comments.author: reporter
reporter
comments.body:
@participant3 https://github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime/releases/tag/v1.20.0 onnxruntime seems to support 3.13? or do you mean that onnxruntime does also have to support 3.13t?

Out of interest or for a better understanding. If you use the gpu variant of onnxruntime, can you expect even more from the free-threading variant?

What is your target platform? (Linux x86?). Then one could focus on these for the creation of compatible wheels.

A better PR for tracking is https://github.com/onnx/onnx/pull/6621 . We could already integrate the creation of mac wheel into the regular main branch. Assistance/Support is always very welcome

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
Hi, thanks for your answer @reporter.
> you need both?

Not necessarily, just 3.13 (not-freethreaded) would be great, thanks for letting us know about the upcoming spring release. About the freethreading, ever since pytorch added support for 3.13t many people in the community are interested to see if there's any performance benefits for their user-case (me included). So that's the reason for asking, benchmarking.
> What is your target platform? (Linux x86?)

Yes, RHEL9 on x86 to be exact.

Thanks again 👍

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: @participant3 did you do some benchmarking for 3.13t?
